title: Street Hoops
premise: A neon-soaked street basketball arcade game where the player launches a single ball from the lower-left side of the court and tries to sink repeated shots into a repositioning hoop for the highest possible streak.
interaction_model: Single-screen drag-and-release physics shooting using mouse or touch; the player pulls to aim and set power, releases to fire, then watches the shot resolve before the next attempt or game over.
objective: Score as many baskets as possible in one run by making successive shots into the hoop before a miss settles and ends the game.
progression: Each made basket increases the score and triggers a short reset into a new shot with the hoop randomized to another position on the right side; difficulty and variation come from changing hoop placement and repeated precision demands rather than from levels or narrative stages.
theme: Late-night urban streetball with futuristic neon styling and an arcade presentation.
mood: Energetic, stylish, replayable, lightly tense, and celebratory on success.
likely_audience: players who enjoy short score-attack sessions
fans of simple physics skill games
confidence_notes: High confidence that this is a drag-to-shoot arcade basketball score-chase game because input, scoring, reset flow, and fail logic are explicit in code.
High confidence in the neon streetball presentation due to the title, city skyline, court glow, and stylized UI.
Moderate confidence in difficulty framing because the challenge emerges from hoop randomization and shot physics rather than a named level system.
recreation_prompt: Create a single-screen browser arcade basketball game called Street Hoops set on a neon-lit nighttime blacktop court with a futuristic city skyline in the background. The player controls one glowing basketball positioned near the lower-left corner and uses mouse or touch drag-and-release controls to aim and set launch power, then releases to shoot. Show an aiming line and dotted trajectory preview while dragging. Simulate simple arcade physics with gravity, capped launch force, wall bounce, floor bounce and friction, and a light backboard collision zone. Place the hoop on the right side of the screen and randomize its height and horizontal placement after every successful basket. Count a score only when the ball falls downward through the rim area. After a made shot, play a celebratory sound, show a quick reaction visual, spawn small particles, increment the score, and reset for the next attempt after a short delay. If the player misses, let the ball bounce and roll until it settles; then end the run, play a fail sound, show a game-over overlay with the final basket count, and offer a replay button. Present everything with glossy glassmorphism menus, bold arcade typography, a compact HUD score display, responsive full-screen canvas rendering, and strong mobile support so the game feels like a fast, replayable, stylish streetball score-attack experience.
